learning_objective: 🎯 Master the behavior of light as rays, understanding how mirrors reflect, lenses refract, and how instruments like microscopes and telescopes manipulate vision!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Light bounces off surfaces. For curved mirrors (concave and convex), the Mirror Formula relates the object distance ($u$), image distance ($v$), and focal length ($f$): $1/v + 1/u = 1/f$.

Light bends when moving between different mediums (like air to water) because its speed changes. If light tries to move from a denser to a rarer medium at a sharp enough angle, it reflects completely internally (TIR). This is how optical fibers work!

Lenses form images by refracting light. Convex lenses converge light, while concave lenses diverge it. The Lens Maker's formula dictates how a lens is manufactured based on the refractive index and radii of curvature.
White light is a mixture of seven colors. A glass prism bends each color by a slightly different amount, splitting the white light into a beautiful spectrum (VIBGYOR).
Microscopes magnify tiny, close objects, while telescopes magnify massive, distant objects. Both use combinations of objective and eyepiece lenses to maximize Angular Magnification.

fun_activity.title: 💧 The Broken Pencil Illusion
fun_activity.instructions: Place a straight pencil half-inside a clear glass of water. Look at it from the side. The pencil looks snapped in half! This is refraction—light from the underwater part of the pencil bends as it enters the air, tricking your eyes.

exam_tips: 📌 Ray diagrams are incomplete without arrows indicating the direction of light. Missing arrows = zero marks!
📌 Master the New Cartesian Sign Convention. Always take the direction of incident light as positive. Object distance ($u$) is almost always negative.
📌 The resolving power of a telescope increases with a larger objective lens diameter.
quick_recap: ⭐ Light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation) in homogeneous mediums.
⭐ Total Internal Reflection causes mirages in deserts and makes diamonds sparkle brilliantly.
⭐ A convex lens acts as a simple magnifying glass when the object is placed within its focal length.
